audience.title: When implementation fails to take hold
audience.subtitle: Typical situations
triggers: After restructuring, growth, or an acquisition, processes and decisions run formally new — but in day-to-day operations the organization still orients itself to the old structures.
Decisions have been made and measures agreed, but coordination loops, silo thinking, and conflicting priorities continue to hold up implementation.
New standards, leadership routines, or responsibilities have been introduced, but gradually lose their binding force in the daily business.

orientation.title:
Clarify briefly.
Decide with confidence.
orientation.text:
What remains unresolved comes at a cost: time in coordination loops, energy in leadership friction, and credibility in decisions that do not land.

If you are wondering whether this is your situation right now, we can clarify that in 15 minutes.

about.title: About me
about.heroTitle: I know operations, leadership, and the pressure behind them.
intro: Not from workshops, but from production, responsibility, and leadership.
Today I work with leaders and organisations in industrial SMEs on exactly these points. Where implementation requires clarity, leadership, and commitment.
about.profileText:
Acceptance arises where language, reality and responsibility align.

My professional path began in an industrial environment and developed through production, leadership, and cross-site responsibility. In parallel, I completed training as an industrial mechanic, further qualification as a state-certified mechanical engineering technician, and studies in business administration and organisational psychology — and today I am working on my doctorate. Always alongside professional practice and close to operational reality.

This combination of plant experience, leadership, and academic engagement shapes my work to this day. My focus is not just on preparing decisions, but on making them effective in practice together with those responsible.
bullets: Over 25 years of operational responsibility in production, logistics, and cross-site leadership
Experience in change, restructuring, and integration situations in industrial environments
Combination of operational practice, leadership responsibility, and academic engagement
Ongoing doctorate on M&A integration, culture, and organisational execution in industrial SMEs
Multilingual collaboration in German, English, Turkish, Spanish, and Arabic

speaking.title: Speaking & Teaching
speaking.intro:
Talks and teaching formats are not a substitute for the actual work. They serve to make connections visible and open up discussion.

I speak about why implementation fails to take hold in organizations and what operational reality has to do with it. Not from theoretical distance, but from responsibility within the organization.
speaking.topicsHint: Click on a topic for details

topics.title: Efficiency and culture in alignment
topics.subtitle: Why transformation fails and how it succeeds
topics.description: Transformation is not a purely technical process. It is always cultural as well. When strategies fail against lived reality, the reason often lies in the tension between pressure for efficiency and loss of identity. The talk shows how both perspectives can be brought together so that change is not only planned, but understood and carried in everyday work.

topics.title: Shopfloor leadership
topics.subtitle: Leadership through rhythm, not actionism
topics.description: Impact emerges where value creation takes place. When leadership on the shop floor is replaced by short-term actionism, the system loses stability. I show how clear routines, metrics, and a reliable leadership rhythm create orientation and make responsibility effective where problems arise.

topics.title: Lean management
topics.subtitle: Impact in everyday work, not a collection of methods
topics.description: Lean is not a toolbox, but a logic of simplification and learning. Many initiatives fail not because methods are missing, but because they do not connect to everyday work. The session focuses on a few levers that stabilize standards, problem solving, and collaboration without turning into a hunt for methods.

topics.title: M&A integration
topics.subtitle: Culture, identity, and operational models that work
topics.description: The economic success of mergers is decided after closing, in collaboration, leadership, and identity. Based on operational practice and applied research, I show how questions of culture and identity can be addressed early and how an operating model can emerge that secures performance without losing cultural DNA.

topics.title: Change governance
topics.subtitle: The operating system of effective implementation
topics.description: Change needs a clear framework. Otherwise ambiguity and friction take over. Change governance is the operating system of transformation: decision paths, roles, rhythm, and communication. The talk shows how governance can be built pragmatically so that decisions take hold, communication builds trust, and new ways of working do not fizzle out.

topics.title: Leadership in transition
topics.subtitle: Role, impact, responsibility
topics.description: In transformation phases, expectations of leadership change significantly, away from the pure expert and toward the shaper of orientation, responsibility, and collaboration. I reflect on how leadership remains effective in uncertainty, how roles are clarified, and how responsibility is placed where it actually has an effect in everyday work.
